    18	### What They Do
    19	
    20	Pre-commit hooks automatically run whenever you execute `git commit`. They perform the following checks:
    21	
    22	1. **Format code** with Prettier
    23	2. **Lint and auto-fix** with ESLint
    24	3. **Type-check** with TypeScript compiler
    25	4. **Run tests** for changed files (backend only, currently)
    26	
    27	### How They Work
    28	
    29	The hooks are managed by [Husky](https://typicode.github.io/husky/) and configured to run [lint-staged](https://github.com/okonet/lint-staged), which only processes files that you've changed. This makes the hooks fast and efficient.
    30	
    31	### Hook Scripts
    32	
    33	- `.husky/pre-commit` - Runs lint-staged on staged files
    34	- `.husky/commit-msg` - Validates commit message format with commitlint
    35	
    36	## TypeScript Strict Mode
    37	
    38	Both backend and frontend use strict TypeScript settings to ensure type safety:
    39	
    40	### Backend (NestJS)
    41	
    42	```json
    43	{
    44	  "strict": true,
    45	  "noImplicitAny": true,
    46	  "strictNullChecks": true,
    47	  "strictBindCallApply": true,
    48	  "noFallthroughCasesInSwitch": true,
    49	  "noImplicitReturns": true,
    50	  "noUnusedLocals": true,
    51	  "noUnusedParameters": true
    52	}
    53	```
    54	
    55	### Frontend (Next.js)
    56	
    57	```json
    58	{
    59	  "strict": true
    60	}
    61	```
    62	
    63	### ESLint Rules
    64	
    65	Backend enforces strict type checking with these rules:
    66	
    67	- `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any`: Error (disallows `any` types)
    68	- `@typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises`: Error (requires handling promises)
    69	- `@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-argument`: Error (prevents unsafe type assertions)
    70	- `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars`: Error (catches unused variables)
    71	- `@typescript-eslint/no-misused-promises`: Error (prevents promise misuse)
    72	- `@typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-type-assertion`: Error (prevents redundant type assertions)
    73	
    74	## Commit Message Format
    75	
    76	All commit messages must follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) specification:
    77	
    78	### Format
    79	
    80	```
    81	<type>(<scope>): <subject>
    82	
    83	<body>
    84	
    85	<footer>
    86	```
    87	
    88	### Types
    89	
    90	- `feat` - A new feature
    91	- `fix` - A bug fix
    92	- `docs` - Documentation changes
    93	- `style` - Code style changes (formatting, etc.)
    94	- `refactor` - Code refactoring
    95	- `perf` - Performance improvements
    96	- `test` - Adding or updating tests
    97	- `chore` - Maintenance tasks
    98	- `revert` - Reverting a previous commit
    99	
   100	### Scopes
   101	
   102	Allowed scopes for this monorepo:
   103	
   104	- `backend` - Changes to the NestJS backend
   105	- `frontend` - Changes to the Next.js frontend
   106	- `root` - Changes to root-level configuration
   107	- `docs` - Documentation changes
   108	- `husky` - Git hooks configuration
   109	- `lint-staged` - Lint-staged configuration
   110	
   111	### Examples
   112	
   113	```bash
   114	feat(backend): add user authentication endpoint
   115	
   116	Implement JWT-based authentication with login and registration endpoints.
   117	
   118	Closes #123
   119	```
   120	
   121	```bash
   122	fix(frontend): resolve navigation bug on mobile devices
   123	
   124	The navigation menu was not closing properly on mobile screens.
   125	```
   126	
   127	```bash
   128	docs: update API documentation
   129	
   130	Added documentation for new authentication endpoints.
   131	```
   132	
   133	### Validation
   134	
   135	Commit messages are automatically validated by commitlint. If your message doesn't follow the format, the commit will be rejected with an error message explaining what's wrong.
   136	
   137	## Linting and Formatting
   138	
   139	### Prettier
   140	
   141	Prettier is configured at the root level (`.prettierrc`) with these settings:
   142	
   143	```json
   144	{
   145	  "singleQuote": true,
   146	  "trailingComma": "all",
   147	  "tabWidth": 2,
   148	  "semi": true,
   149	  "printWidth": 100,
   150	  "arrowParens": "always",
   151	  "endOfLine": "auto"
   152	}
   153	```
   154	
   155	### ESLint
   156	
   157	Both backend and frontend have ESLint configured:
   158	
   159	- **Backend**: TypeScript ESLint with strict rules
   160	- **Frontend**: Next.js ESLint with Prettier integration
   161	
   162	### Running Manually
   163	
   164	You can run linting and formatting manually:
   165	
   166	```bash
   167	# Format all files
   168	npm run format
   169	
   170	# Lint all files
   171	npm run lint
   172	
   173	# Lint and auto-fix
   174	npm run lint:fix
   175	
   176	# Type-check all files
   177	npm run type-check
   178	```
   179	
   180	### Workspace-specific commands
   181	
   182	```bash
   183	# Backend
   184	cd backend
   185	npm run lint
   186	npm run format
   187	
   188	# Frontend
   189	cd frontend
   190	npm run lint
   191	npm run format
   192	```
   193	
   194	## Testing Requirements
   195	
   196	### Backend Tests
   197	
   198	Backend uses Jest for unit and e2e testing. Tests are automatically run for changed files during pre-commit.
   199	
   200	```bash
   201	# Run all tests
   202	cd backend
   203	npm test
   204	
   205	# Run tests in watch mode
   206	npm run test:watch
   207	
   208	# Run tests with coverage
   209	npm run test:cov
   210	
   211	# Run e2e tests
   212	npm run test:e2e
   213	```
   214	
   215	### Test Configuration
   216	
   217	Tests are configured to:
   218	
   219	- Run only tests related to changed files (`--findRelatedTests`)
   220	- Stop on first failure (`--bail`)
   221	- Use up to 4 workers for parallel execution (`--maxWorkers=4`)
   222	
   223	### Frontend Tests
   224	
   225	Frontend tests are not yet configured but will be added in the future.
   226	
   227	## Troubleshooting
   228	
   229	### Pre-commit Hooks Not Running
   230	
   231	**Problem**: Hooks don't execute when you commit.
   232	
   233	**Solutions**:
   234	
   235	1. Ensure hooks are installed:
   236	
   237	   ```bash
   238	   npm run prepare
   239	   ```
   240	
   241	2. Check if hooks are executable:
   242	
   243	   ```bash
   244	   ls -la .husky/
   245	   ```
   246	
   247	   The files should have execute permissions (`-rwxr-xr-x`).
   248	
   249	3. If hooks were bypassed with `--no-verify`, reinstall them:
   250	   ```bash
   251	   npm run prepare
   252	   ```
   253	
   254	### Commit Message Rejected
   255	
   256	**Problem**: commitlint rejects your commit message.
   257	
   258	**Solutions**:
   259	
   260	1. Check the error message for specific issues
   261	2. Ensure format: `<type>(<scope>): <subject>`
   262	3. Keep subject under 72 characters
   263	4. Use one of the allowed types and scopes
   264	
   265	**Example of invalid message**:
   266	
   267	```
   268	Added new feature
   269	```
   270	
   271	**Correct format**:
   272	
   273	```
   274	feat(backend): add user authentication
   275	```
   276	
   277	### Linting Errors Blocking Commit
   278	
   279	**Problem**: ESLint errors prevent committing.
   280	
   281	**Solutions**:
   282	
   283	1. Run lint with auto-fix:
   284	
   285	   ```bash
   286	   npm run lint:fix
   287	   ```
   288	
   289	2. Fix errors manually in your editor
   290	3. If you must commit temporarily (not recommended):
   291	   ```bash
   292	   git commit --no-verify -m "your message"
   293	   ```
   294	
   295	### Type Errors Blocking Commit
   296	
   297	**Problem**: TypeScript type errors prevent committing.
   298	
   299	**Solutions**:
   300	
   301	1. Run type-check to see all errors:
   302	
   303	   ```bash
   304	   npm run type-check
   305	   ```
   306	
   307	2. Fix type errors by:
   308	   - Adding proper type annotations
   309	   - Using `unknown` instead of `any`
   310	   - Fixing type mismatches
   311	
   312	3. For temporary suppression (use sparingly):
   313	   ```typescript
   314	   // @ts-expect-error - TODO: fix this type error
   315	   const data = someFunction();
   316	   ```
   317	
   318	### Tests Failing on Commit
   319	
   320	**Problem**: Tests fail during pre-commit hook.
   321	
   322	**Solutions**:
   323	
   324	1. Run tests manually to see full output:
   325	
   326	   ```bash
   327	   cd backend
   328	   npm test -- --bail --findRelatedTests
   329	   ```
   330	
   331	2. Fix failing tests
   332	3. If tests are unrelated to your changes, skip them temporarily:
   333	   ```bash
   334	   git commit --no-verify -m "your message"
   335	   ```
   336	
   337	### Hooks Too Slow
   338	
   339	**Problem**: Pre-commit hooks take too long to run.
   340	
   341	**Solutions**:
   342	
   343	1. Check which files are being staged:
   344	
   345	   ```bash
   346	   git diff --cached --name-only
   347	   ```
   348	
   349	2. Unstage files you don't want to commit yet:
   350	
   351	   ```bash
   352	   git reset HEAD <file>
   353	   ```
   354	
   355	3. For large changes, consider splitting into smaller commits
   356	
   357	4. If absolutely necessary, bypass hooks (not recommended):
   358	   ```bash
   359	   git commit --no-verify -m "your message"
   360	   ```
   361	
   362	### Prettier Formatting Issues
   363	
   364	**Problem**: Prettier reformats code unexpectedly.
   365	
   366	**Solutions**:
   367	
   368	1. Check `.prettierrc` settings at project root
   369	2. Ensure your editor uses the same Prettier configuration
   370	3. For specific files that shouldn't be formatted, add to `.prettierignore`
   371	
   372	### ESLint and Prettier Conflicts
   373	
   374	**Problem**: ESLint and Prettier have conflicting rules.
   375	
   376	**Solutions**:
   377	
   378	1. This project uses `eslint-config-prettier` to disable conflicting ESLint rules
   379	2. If conflicts persist, check your ESLint configuration
   380	3. Ensure Prettier plugin is loaded after other ESLint configs
   381	
   382	## Best Practices
   383	
   384	### Before Committing
   385	
   386	1. **Stage only what you need**: Only stage files you want to commit
   387	2. **Run checks manually**: Use `npm run lint` and `npm run type-check` before committing
   388	3. **Write good commit messages**: Follow Conventional Commits format
   389	4. **Keep commits focused**: One logical change per commit
   390	5. **Test your changes**: Ensure tests pass before committing
   391	
   392	### Writing Code
   393	
   394	1. **Use TypeScript types**: Avoid `any` types, use proper type annotations
   395	2. **Follow naming conventions**:
   396	   - Classes: `PascalCase`
   397	   - Functions/variables: `camelCase`
   398	   - Constants: `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE`
   399	3. **Write tests**: Add tests for new features and bug fixes
   400	4. **Keep functions small**: Single responsibility principle
   401	5. **Use meaningful names**: Self-documenting code
   402	
   403	### Working with Hooks
   404	
   405	1. **Don't bypass hooks**: Only use `--no-verify` in emergencies
   406	2. **Fix issues immediately**: Don't let linting errors accumulate
   407	3. **Learn from errors**: Understand why hooks are failing
   408	4. **Ask for help**: If you're stuck, consult the team
   409	
   410	## FAQ
   411	
   412	**Q: Can I disable pre-commit hooks?**
   413	
   414	A: Yes, but it's not recommended. Use `git commit --no-verify` to bypass hooks. This should only be done in emergencies or for WIP commits.
   415	
   416	**Q: Why are my commits rejected?**
   417	
   418	A: Check the error message. Common reasons:
   419	
   420	- Invalid commit message format
   421	- Linting errors
   422	- Type errors
   423	- Failing tests
   424	
   425	**Q: How do I fix `any` type errors?**
   426	
   427	A: Replace `any` with proper types:
   428	
   429	- Use `unknown` for truly unknown data
   430	- Create interfaces or types for your data
   431	- Use type guards for runtime checks
   432	
   433	**Q: Can I change the Prettier configuration?**
   434	
   435	A: Yes, edit `.prettierrc` at the project root. Changes will affect all developers, so discuss with the team first.
   436	
   437	**Q: What if I need to commit code with temporary errors?**
   438	
   439	A: Use `git commit --no-verify -m "your message"`. Add a TODO comment to fix the errors later.
   440	
   441	**Q: How do I add new commit types or scopes?**
   442	
   443	A: Edit `commitlint.config.js` to add new types to `type-enum` or new scopes to `scope-enum`.
   444	
   445	**Q: Why are tests running on my frontend changes?**
   446	
   447	A: Frontend tests are not yet configured. Only backend tests run during pre-commit. This will be added in the future.
   448	
   449	**Q: Can I run hooks manually?**
   450	
   451	A: Yes, run `npx lint-staged` to execute the pre-commit hook manually.
   452	
   453	**Q: How do I check if hooks are installed?**
   454	
   455	A: Run `ls -la .husky/` to see the hook scripts. They should be executable.
   456	
   457	**Q: What's the difference between `npm run lint` and `npm run lint:fix`?**
   458	
   459	A: `npm run lint` checks for errors, `npm run lint:fix` automatically fixes fixable issues.
   460	
   461	## Additional Resources
   462	
   463	- [Husky Documentation](https://typicode.github.io/husky/)
   464	- [lint-staged Documentation](https://github.com/okonet/lint-staged)
   465	- [commitlint Documentation](https://commitlint.js.org/)
   466	- [Prettier Documentation](https://prettier.io/)
   467	- [ESLint Documentation](https://eslint.org/)
   468	- [TypeScript Documentation](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)
   469	- [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
   470	- [NestJS Documentation](https://docs.nestjs.com/)
   471	- [Next.js Documentation](https://nextjs.org/docs)
   472	
   473	## Getting Help
   474	
   475	If you encounter issues not covered in this guide:
   476	
   477	1. Check the error message carefully
   478	2. Search the documentation for related topics
   479	3. Ask a team member for help
   480	4. Create an issue in the project repository
   481	
   482	Remember: The code quality automation system is here to help you write better code, not to hinder your productivity. Embrace it, and you'll see the benefits in code quality and team collaboration.
